title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-evelyn-wright
content:
Goal: qualify and open conversation with Acme Ads (adtech platform). Explore partnership for Dedicated offering (reserved capacity) + co-marketing for their enterprise customers. Target intro -> 30-min discovery -> pilot (3 months).

Quick account profile (public + notes):
- Company: Acme Ads (acmeads.com) — mid-market adtech, heavy real-time bidding, onboarding agencies + retail chains.
- HQ: SF. Estimated revenue: $120M. Funding: Series D (2023).
- Technical indicators: Open positions for ML infra (LinkedIn), blog posts on latency and bid optimization, using GPU capacity on AWS (mentions of p3/p4 in infra blog).
- Potential persona(s): Head of ML Infrastructure (Emily Park), Director of Infrastructure (Rajesh Menon), Head of Ads Product (Sofia Martinez), Platform Eng manager (internal platform).
- Why Redwood matters: deterministic token-level cost + dedicated GPU pools + private/VPC options for agency data privacy. Also rollouts + fallback are attractive for production ads workloads where downtime = revenue.

Notes from past public signals / tech stack:
- They cite requirements: <50ms tail latency for scoring, need batching for throughput but can't sacrifice bidding latency.
- Use cases: creative generation + real-time scoring + taxonomy tagging for campaigns.
- Security/compliance: GDPR, SOC2 mentioned on careers page. Might care about private deployment or VPC and KMS integration.

Hypothesis: Acme will evaluate on three axes: latency SLA, cost (per-request), and integration effort. They will prefer low-risk trials (dedicated pool with predictable billing).

Outbound angle options (pick 1 or test A/B):
A) Cost + deterministic throughput: "Cut inference cost per conversion by 30% with predictable reserved capacity" (email subject). Emphasize unit economics and dedicated pools.
B) Reliability + graceful degradation: "Keep bidding live during traffic spikes — automatic fallbacks and model variants". Highlight rollouts + canary + fallback.
C) Security + isolation: "Bring inference into your VPC with Redwood Private". For enterprise compliance folks.

Cold email draft - Sequence A (short + product-led):
Subject: Quick win for Acme Ads' bidding latency
Hi Emily —
I noticed Acme Ads is optimizing real-time bidding latency (your blog post from Nov). We help teams like yours move from ad-hoc GPU endpoints to predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) while cutting per-query cost via caching + batching heuristics.
Any interest in a 20-min chat to see if a reserved pool (1–2 nodes) could lower your inference cost and give a 99th % latency SLO? Happy to share a quick TCO calc.
—Evelyn

LinkedIn touchpoint (short):
- Connect note: "Emily — love Acme’s latency work. I help infra teams stabilize inference costs/SLAs. Quick intro?"

Warm intro request template (ask internal):
Hi Noah — do you have any tie-ins to Acme Ads? Would appreciate an intro to Emily Park / Rajesh Menon. Quick 2-line ask I can use: "Intro to Emily at Acme to discuss inference SLOs + cost optimization for production bidding workloads."

Key objections and suggested responses (short bullets):
- Objection: "We run on our own infra; can't move to hosted."
  Response: "We support private/VPC and on-prem packages + KMS/HSM integrations. Dedicated can run in their cloud with private control plane; minimal data egress."
- Objection: "Latency can't tolerate batching."
  Response: "Redwood supports latency-aware batching and continuous KV cache so hot paths have near-zero extra latency; we can demo 99th% p99 numbers on a small pilot."
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in / migration cost."
  Response: "Model versioning + canary rollouts make migration incremental. Fallback to current endpoint during rollout. Also provide tooling to snapshot KV cache and warm pipelines."
- Objection: "Cost concerns for Dedicated commit."
  Response: "Offer pilot with limited reserved nodes + burst-to-cloud; work with finance on trial credits and a structured pilot with defined SLO/ROI checkpoints."

Pilot proposal (initial internal sketch to discuss with product):
- Duration: 8–12 weeks (shorter if we do a narrow scope).
- Scope options: 1) scoring model for auctions (focus on p99 latency) OR 2) creative generation batch jobs (throughput focus).
- Minimum commitment: 2 dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA A10/NVIDIA H100?), plus telemetry + tracing hook.
- Success metrics: p99 latency target <50ms, per-inference cost reduction >=20%, 99.9% availability during business hours.
- Data/security: VPC mode recommended for agencies; KMS for keys, audit logs enabled.

Meeting agenda (30-min discovery):
1) 5 min intros + context on current infra/constraints
2) 7 min current traffics/latency/cost pain points (metrics)
3) 8 min how they run models today (hosting, model size, caching)
4) 7 min discuss pilot options + success metrics
5) 3 min next steps / decision maker alignment

Metrics / ask to bring to meeting (what to request in advance):
- sample qps & p95/p99 latency for scoring endpoints
- current infra (instance types, autoscaling behavior)
- annual inference spend estimate (approx)
- top 2-3 models used in production (size, framework)

Open questions to research before outreach:
- Confirm if they use AWS/GCP and which instance families (p3/p4/a100/h100) — helps shape Dedicated offering and pricing.
- Find any public PRs or repos referencing ONNX / Triton / custom kernels — hints at model infra.
- Look for conference talks (LATAM adtech conf?) where they mentioned real-time constraints.

Internal asks / blockers:
- Pricing sheet for mid-market Dedicated pilots (1–3 nodes) + standard pilot credits (ask FinOps).
- Engineering contact for rapid pilot: who owns private/VPC packaging? (Priya?)

Follow-ups (TODOs):
- [ ] Update TCO calc template with A10/H100 numbers (ask infra team).
- [ ] Draft two A/B email subject lines and run small sequence test.
- [ ] Ask Noah for intro; if no, find mutual connection on LinkedIn.
- [ ] Add Acme to partner-tracker spreadsheet (sheet id: partners-2025).

Scratch/brainstorm subject lines (test):
- "Reduce inference spend for bids at scale"
- "Keep auctions live during traffic spikes"
- "Dedicated inference for adtech: cut cost + control latency"

Notes to self: keep outbound short, technical, and outcome-focused. For platform folks, lead with latency/cost + deployment flexibility. For product/ops, lead with reliability + canary/fallback stories. Use real numbers where possible (p99 reductions) — customers respond to quantified wins.

End.
